title: EOS diagnostic report
description: What an EOS tool writes to stdout with --json: one verdict, the problems behind it, and the command that reproduces it. The problem item is the same one `eos check --json` uses for a gate's failing checks, so every EOS verdict is read the same way. (ADR-010)

tool.description: The tool that produced the report.

status.description: PASS: verified. NOT_APPLICABLE: nothing was verified because there is nothing to verify — never read it as PASS. FAIL: checked, and wrong. BLOCKED: could not be checked because a precondition is missing (for example a toolchain). ERROR: the configuration itself could not be evaluated. Worst first: ERROR > BLOCKED > FAIL, the gate engine's order.

exitCode.description: The process exit code. --json never changes it: 0 for PASS and NOT_APPLICABLE, 1 otherwise.

summary.description: The verdict line the human mode prints.

notes.description: Facts that are neither problems nor the verdict (steps not declared, what was skipped).

rerunCommand.description: The command that reproduces this verdict.

details.description: Tool-specific facts. Open by design: everything a consumer needs to act on is in the fields above.

level.description: error: this problem decides the verdict. warning: reported, never blocking.

code.description: A stable identifier: a validator code (P3, D5, S13) or a gate check id (tests-executed).

status.description: The verdict this problem implies. Present on every error.

gate.description: The gate whose check this is, when the problem comes from a gate.

artifact.description: The file the problem is about, when there is one.
